newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli high-tech firms seek more research funds.
newsitem.headline: Israeli high-tech firms seek more research funds.

text.p: Requests by Israeli high-tech firms for state grants for research and development rose in monetary terms by 21 percent in the first quarter compared with the same period last year, official figures showed on Sunday.
The Chief Scientist's Office in the Industry and Trade Ministry said high-tech firms asked for $586 million in grants in the first quarter against $484 million in the the first three months of 1996.

An official statement attributed the increase in grant requests to a rise in foreign investment, to $1.2 billion in 1996 from $240 million in 1995, in Israeli high-tech companies eligible for funds from the Chief Scientist's Office. The figures do not include share offerings in Israel and abroad.
But the statement said the ministry was finding it hard to meet grant requests because of a 10 percent erosion in its 1997 research and development budget.

"This is hurting the capabilities of high-tech industry, which represents Israel's main chance for economic independence, and the industry's ability to boost significantly its sales -- aimed mainly at export markets," the statement said.
The Chief Scientist's Office said it planned to ask the Treasury to increase the research and development budget for 1997.
